'''John Hubert Potter''' (1927 – 17 July 2017) was an English chemist who falsely claimed to be a [[Special Operations Executive]] agent who worked with the [[French resistance]] during [[World War II]].

==Early life and family==
John Hubert Potter was born in [[Camberwell]], south London, in 1927.<ref name=times2/><ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QV3V-1BYZ John H Potter England and Wales Birth Registration Index.] Family Search. Retrieved 4 October 2017.</ref> He was born with a [[club foot]] which was later corrected.<ref name=times1/><ref name=worth/>

Potter married, first, Olive with whom he had six children, Anne, Roy, Hugh, Neil, Nigel, and Mark. After a divorce, he married Mildred in 1976, a hairdresser he met while travelling in Vienna in 1970.<ref name=times2/>

==Career==
Potter had a career as a research chemist and salesman. He lived with his second wife Mildred in Belgium and France before retiring to Sussex, England.<ref name=times2/>

==False claims==
Potter falsely claimed to be a Special Operations Executive agent who worked with the French Resistance during the Second World War under the name Henri Dufour, an 18 year old who he said had been killed in an air raid in northern France while working for the resistance. Potter claimed to have been asked by the SOE to take Dufour's place in 1942 due to his language skills and because he was the right age and both had a club foot. According to Potter, he worked with the resistance throughout the war, was periodically flown back to Britain to brief [[Winston Churchill]], who gave him a glass of brandy, had an affair with a French woman named Yvette, entered [[Dachau concentration camp]] with the Americans, and worked as a liaison officer to defend a chemist accused of war crimes at the [[Nuremberg trials]].<ref name=times2>[https://www.thetimes.com/world/europe/article/john-potter-the-fantasist-soe-spy-who-fooled-his-own-wife-9qwg8vrsg John Potter, the fantasist ‘spy’ who fooled his own wife.] Simon de Bruxelles, ''The Times'', 30 September 2017. Retrieved 4 October 2017.</ref><ref name=times1/> He also claimed to have an OBE awarded after the war and a first class degree from the [[University of London]].<ref name=times1/> His memoirs were self-published in 2009 as ''Within the Shadows'' under the pen-name of Ernest Tarrant.<ref name=worth>[http://www.worthingherald.co.uk/news/courageous-teen-war-spy-passes-away-1-8094113 'Courageous' teen war spy passes away.] James Butler, ''Worthing Herald'', 9 August 2017. Retrieved 4 October 2017.</ref><ref>[https://www.authorhouse.co.uk/BookStore/BookDetail.aspx?Book=277366 ''Within the Shadows'' by Ernest Tarrant.] authorhouse. Retrieved 4 October 2017.</ref>

The claims were only exposed as false after his death when he received an obituary in a local paper ''The Worthing Herald'',<ref name=worth/> as well as in national papers ''[[The Daily Express|The Express]]'',<ref>[http://www.express.co.uk/news/uk/839930/world-war-two-winston-churchill-adviser-john-potter-spy Revealed: WW2 hero who secretly advised Winston Churchill.]''Express'', 11 August 2017. Retrieved 4 October 2017.</ref> ''[[Daily Mirror|The Mirror]]'',<ref>[https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/ww2-spy-who-reported-winston-10971410 WW2 spy who reported to Winston Churchill and kept incredible military life a secret for 50 years dies aged 93.] Stephen White, ''Mirror'', 11 August 2017. Retrieved 4 October 2017.</ref> and ''[[The Times]]'',<ref name=times1/> all of which accepted his story. ''The Times'' subsequently retracted its obituary in a new article after doubt was thrown on the content in reader feedback.<ref name=times2/> Potter's son Neil, an Anglican priest and vicar of the church in Camborne, Cornwall, was quoted as saying "To the best of my brothers' and my sister's knowledge none of this ever happened ... He was too young to serve in the war. This was a claim he made up to impress his second wife and we cringed when we heard it. It is not the only thing he lied about."<ref name=times2/>

==Death==
Potter died from the effects of dementia on 17 July 2017<ref name=times1>"John Potter", ''The Times'', 20 September 2017, p. 56.</ref> at St. Michael's Nursing Home.<ref name=johns/> The funeral was at [[Worthing Crematorium]] followed by a memorial service at [[St Andrew's Church, West Tarring|St Andrew's Church]], [[West Tarring]].<ref name=johns>[http://announcements.johnstonpress.co.uk/obituaries/littlehamptongazette-uk/obituary.aspx?pid=186205974 John Potter.] ''Littlehampton Gazette''/''Worthing Herald'', 27 July 2017. Retrieved 4 October 2017.</ref> Despite evidence that has emerged since his death, Mildred Potter maintains that her husband's story of wartime heroism is completely true, saying "you cannot make up all those details".<ref name=times2/>
